decisions.reason: The question asks whether SiT captures real-world pedestrian–robot interactions. It omits how the dataset supports pedestrian perception and motion prediction for social navigation.

The method mentions a mobile robot and indoor and outdoor scenes. It omits manual operation, crowded locations in Seoul, the two 3D LiDARs and five cameras, pulse-per-second synchronization, and 360-degree camera coverage.
The method gives 20-second sequences at 10 Hz. It omits the counts of scenes, images, and point-cloud frames, as well as 2D and 3D box annotations, object IDs, and multilayer semantic maps.
The poster omits ego-motion compensation and the use of distinct scenes in the training, validation, and test subsets.
The finding and caption define both interaction criteria and report that SiT has more instances satisfying both. Panel (b) names Waymo Open, Argoverse 2, and nuScenes in its legend.
The poster omits the detection and tracking baselines, the center-distance thresholds used to calculate detection mAP, and the tracking metrics.

The method gives 9 seconds of trajectory data per sample but omits the 2-second history and 7-second forecast split, minimum ADE and FDE at 5 and 20 candidates, the forecasting baselines, and the reported semantic-map gains.
The poster omits the 7-second end-to-end benchmark from raw sensor data to future 3D boxes and trajectories, the compared models, and the four evaluation metrics.
The poster omits the authors’ statement that time constraints prevented collection at the scale of hundreds of thousands of frames.

ratings.notes: The figure legends and axis labels are readable at the supplied image size, though small relative to the poster text. The headings and placement of the figure below the finding make the reading order clear. The checklist confirms the 20-second duration, 10 Hz sampling rate, and 2-meter threshold. Its 2-second history and 7-second future are consistent with the stated 9-second sample duration. The supplied evidence does not establish whether “significantly higher” refers to a formal statistical test.

decisions.reason: The question covers real-world interactions between pedestrians and a mobile robot but omits how SiT supports pedestrian perception and motion prediction for social navigation.

The method mentions a mobile robot and indoor and outdoor scenes. It omits manual operation, crowded locations in Seoul, the two 3D LiDARs and five cameras, pulse-per-second synchronization, and 360-degree camera coverage.
The method gives 20-second clips at 10 Hz but omits the 60 scenes, 60K images, 12K point-cloud frames, 2D and 3D box annotations, object IDs, and multilayer semantic maps.
The poster omits robot ego-motion compensation and the use of different scenes for training, validation, and testing.

The finding states that SiT has more instances meeting both criteria. The finding and caption define shared semantic space and proximity within 2 meters, and the figure identifies Waymo Open, Argoverse 2, and nuScenes.
The poster omits the 3D detection and tracking baselines, center-distance AP thresholds and their role in mAP, and the tracking metrics.

The method gives 9 seconds of trajectory data but omits the 2-second history and 7-second forecast, minimum ADE and FDE over 5 and 20 candidates, the three baselines, and the reduction in displacement errors with semantic maps for Y-Net and NSP-SFM.
The poster omits the raw-sensor benchmark for predicting future 3D boxes and trajectories over 7 seconds, the Fast and Furious and FutureDet baselines, and the four evaluation metrics.
The poster omits the authors’ statement that time constraints prevented collection at the scale of hundreds of thousands of frames.

ratings.notes: The title, question, method, and key finding are easy to follow. The small axis labels and legends require close reading, and the abbreviated ‘Sharing&Proxi.’ label is easier to understand with the caption. The 9-second duration is consistent with the checklist’s 2-second history plus 7-second forecast. The missing breakdown reduces C07 coverage without adding a numerical error. No layout defects are visible in the supplied export.
